content.content:
name = 'agents'
description = 'A home for your AI agents'
version = '0.28.0'
bin = { agents: './dist/cli.js' }
repository.url = 'git+https://github.com/cloudflare/agents.git'
readme = '# agents\n' +
  '\n' +
  '![npm install agents](../../assets/npm-install-agents.svg)\n' +
  '\n' +
  '**Build software that thinks and does.**\n' +
  '\n' +
  "Persistent AI agents on Cloudflare's global network. They remember context, reason through problems, schedule their own work, and take action—all without you managing servers.\n" +
  '\n' +
  '```sh\n' +
  'npm create cloudflare@latest -- --template cloudflare/agents-starter\n' +
  '```\n' +
  '\n' +
  'Or add to an existing project:\n' +
  '\n' +
  '```sh\n' +
  'npm install agents\n' +
  '```\n' +
  '\n' +
  'The examples below use `@callable()` decorators. Vite projects must extend\n' +
  '`agents/tsconfig` and add the `agents/vite` plugin; other bundlers must support\n' +
  'TC39 decorators (`2023-11`). See\n' +
  '[Adding Agents to an Existing Project](../../docs/agents/adding-to-existing-project.md#4-configure-typescript-and-vite).\n' +
  '\n' +
  '---\n' +
  '\n' +
  '## Why Agents, Why Now\n' +
  '\n' +
  'LLMs can reason, plan, and use tools—but they need infrastructure that matches their capabilities. Traditional serverless is stateless and ephemeral. Agents are persistent and purposeful.\n' +
  '\n' +
  '```\n' +
  'From request handlers    →  to autonomous entities\n' +
  'From stateless functions →  to persistent intelligence\n' +
  '\n' +
  'Traditional serverless:  Request → Response → Gone\n' +
  'Agents:                  Thinking, remembering, acting — continuously\n' +
  '```\n' +
  '\n' +
  '**Pay only when active.** Agents hibernate between requests. You can have millions of agents—one per user, per session, per game room—each costs nothing when idle.\n' +
  '\n' +
  'Built on Cloudflare Durable Objects, agents run globally, close to your users, with persistent state that survives restarts.\n' +
  '\n' +
  '---\n' +
  '\n' +
  '## Quick Example\n' +
  '\n' +
  'A counter agent with real-time state sync and callable methods:\n' +
  '\n' +
  '```typescript\n' +
  '// server.ts\n' +
  'import { Agent, callable } from "agents";\n' +
  '\n' +
  'export type State = { count: number };\n' +
  '\n' +
  'export class CounterAgent extends Agent<Env, State> {\n' +
  '  initialState: State = { count: 0 };\n' +
  '\n' +
  '  @callable()\n' +
  '  increment() {\n' +
  '    this.setState({ count: this.state.count + 1 });\n' +
  '    return this.state.count;\n' +
  '  }\n' +
  '\n' +
  '  @callable()\n' +
  '  decrement() {\n' +
  '    this.setState({ count: this.state.count - 1 });\n' +
  '    return this.state.count;\n' +
  '  }\n' +
  '}\n' +
  '```\n' +
  '\n' +
  '```tsx\n' +
  '// client.tsx\n' +
  'import { useAgent } from "agents/react";\n' +
  'import { useState } from "react";\n' +
  'import type { CounterAgent, State } from "./server";\n' +

The visible portion defines one subcommand, **`tui`**. The page is truncated, so other subcommands may exist in the omitted code.

**What `tui` does:** It opens a terminal interface that follows a conversation on an agent's Web Channel. The usage text reads:

> "Usage: agents tui <url> [--as <participant>] [--header <name=value>]..."

It accepts `--as`, which sets the `as` query parameter, and a repeatable `--header` flag for the WebSocket upgrade. The parser handles `--as` in this way:

```js
if(o===`--as`)r=c();
```

Inside the interface, the help text lists slash commands the agent may support: `/new`, `/fork`, `/reset [note]`, `/conversations`, and `/switch <id>`. These are in-session commands, not CLI subcommands.

**Cloudflare Access:** If the URL sits behind Cloudflare Access, the tool fetches a token through `cloudflared`. The help text says, "A URL behind Access gets a token from cloudflared, which logs in through" the browser on first use. Alternatively, `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID` and `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET` can supply a service token.

content.text:
`npx agents tui` opens a chat interface in your terminal for an AI agent built with Cloudflare's Agents SDK (the npm package `agents`). The usage is `agents tui <url> [--as <participant>] [--header <name=value>]...`. It connects to a running agent's web channel over a WebSocket at that URL, and you can then follow and join the conversation from the terminal.

- **`--as`** sets which participant you appear as.
- **`--header`** adds a header to the connection request, and you can repeat it.
- **Slash commands:** inside the session, the agent may support commands like `/new`, `/fork`, `/reset`, `/conversations` and `/switch <id>` for managing conversations.
- **Cloudflare Access:** if the URL is behind Access, it gets a login token through `cloudflared`, which opens your browser the first time. You can instead set `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID` and `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET` to use a service token.

I got this from the help text in the package's CLI code (version 0.28.0, the latest on npm) via a web-page fetch tool that read only the first third of the file. I didn't run the command, and other details may be in the part it didn't read.
